pr_title: Link Project to Repository or Team Command
pr_body:
<!--
  Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!
  To reference an open issue, please write this in your description: `Fixes #NUMBER`
-->

Fixes #7849 
This PR implements `gh project link` command. Here are some examples:
```bash
# Link project to a repo
gh project link 1 --repo my-repo

# Link project to a team
gh project link 1 --team my-team

# Unlink project from a repo
gh project unlink 1 --repo my-repo

# Unlink project from a team
gh project unlink 1 --team my-team
```
pr_comments: @williammartin The support for directory-based repo and `GH_REPO` has been implemented, checkout the latest changes 🚀

This is looking very close 🎉 . I've played around with the UX today and I think there's just a few things that could do with some love.

Firstly, adding some text to the help description and example to both commands demonstrating that if no `--team` or `--repo` is provided, it will attempt to use the base repo. I think as a follow up we should consider making the error message better if neither `--repo` or `--team` are provided **and** we're not in a git repo, but I think that's a problem across the board with commands that expect to be in a repo so I don't expect you to handle it here.

Secondly, I really don't think that the `json` exporter is providing much value here. Here's what it looks like for `link`ing a team and repo:

```
➜  gh project link --format json --owner williammartin-test-org --team a-team 1
{
  "ID": "T_kwDOB-vozM4AeSfB",
  "URL": "https://github.com/orgs/williammartin-test-org/teams/a-team"
}
```

```
➜  gh project link --format json --owner williammartin-test-org --repo test-repo 1
{
  "Name": "test-repo",
  "ID": "R_kgDOJgN1OA",
  "URL": "https://github.com/williammartin-test-org/test-repo"
}
```

I don't find it to be particularly useful information. It's also not necessarily the information they might want to see, maybe they want to see the project data rather than the repository or team? I don't think we should be tying our CLI UX to an individual query like this. If we remove this then we can also trim down our graphql data transfer because we no longer need to ask for the `Team` or `Repository` as part of the mutation.

If people ask for this data to be machine readable in the future then we can easily add it back without handcuffing ourselves into supporting it forever now. Make sense?
@williammartin It makes sense not to print the `Team` or `Repository` as a result. Maybe the `--format json` option can be removed for now. Thanks for your feedback!
Yeh I think I would just remove `--format`. I like the human readable text that is displayed though. It might even be useful if we have the project name to display that too?
@williammartin I've made some changes, checkout the latest updates. Thanks!

@williammartin I have an idea. How about eliminating the use of `--owner` and instead using `--repo owner/repo` or `--team org/team`? This approach is more common and is less likely to confuse users

---

> I have an idea. How about eliminating the use of --owner and instead using --repo owner/repo or --team org/team? This 
> approach is more common and is less likely to confuse users

What I'm not sure about here is that all the other `gh project` commands take the `--owner` flag to help disambiguate. It seems unfortunate to change that.

Do you think there is an issue with supporting both `--repo owner/repo` and `--repo repo` (and the same for team)?

> Should the assert.Equal also be replaced with require.Equal?

I prefer this, but I don't mind. `require.Error` and `require.NoError` are important because it almost never makes sense to see the result of assertions after them because it means something has gone extremely wrong in the test and the following assertions will just be noise. Sometimes it makes sense to see the values of other assertion failures together.

> Do you think there is an issue with supporting both --repo owner/repo and --repo repo (and the same for team)?

No, I can try to implement this feature
@williammartin I have made some changes, take a look at the latest commit!

issue_context.title: Link Project to Repository Command
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

I'd like to be able to link a project to a repository from the CLI.

### Proposed solution

A new command, `gh project link [<number>] [<repository>]` which links the project to a repository. Uses the `linkProjectV2ToRepository` GraphQL mutation for implementation.

Will allow users to link a project to a repository from the CLI
comments: @dsanders11 This seems like a solid idea and a workflow we should support. I looked at `updateProjectV2` mutation and I don't see any way to link a repository, can you share the docs where you saw this was possible?

> I looked at `updateProjectV2` mutation and I don't see any way to link a repository, can you share the docs where you saw this was possible?

Whoops, that was a copy-and-paste error on my end, I meant to refer to `linkProjectV2ToRepository`. I'll update the issue description.

There's also `linkProjectV2ToTeam` and unlink equivalents for both of those, so that should probably be handled for completeness.

Maybe it should just be options added to `gh project edit` as your earlier comment mentioned - maybe similar to adding/removing reviewers with `gh pr edit`? Maybe options like `--link-to-repository`, `--link-to-team`, and `--unlink-from-repository` and `--unlink-from-team`.

Just some off the cuff thoughts, haven't thought much about what form it takes, just that the functionality would be useful. 🙂

@dsanders11 Thanks for the clarification. I agree, now that we know it is available from the API, that this would be a useful feature. As for where the feature belongs, I have thought a bit more about it and I think a dedicated `project link` command makes more sense then shoehorning this feature into `project edit`. A dedicated command can also support linking to a team as well as a repository as you mentioned.
